activities.title: Balance Shapes
activities.summary: Explore steady body shapes and choose how to make them easier to hold.

participation.adult_role: Demonstrate comfortable shapes, stay nearby and help the child adjust.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level, firm area with space to stretch without contact.
The activity stays on the ground away from traffic and moving equipment.
setup: Begin with both feet on the ground in a comfortable position.
Explain that steady shapes can be small and both feet can stay down.
Agree that either person can change a shape, pause or stop whenever wanted.

5-7.challenge: Explore one steady shape at a time with both feet grounded.

steps.instruction: Keep both feet down and stretch your arms sideways.
steps.parent_prompt: Show a small comfortable stretch and check room around each person.

steps.instruction: Bring your arms close and make a smaller shape.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep both feet still; a smaller arm position is enough.

steps.instruction: Choose a shape that feels steady to you.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite the child to keep or change either demonstrated arm position.

5-7.ending: Return to a comfortable resting position and finish together.

8-10.challenge: Compare two arm positions and notice which feels steadier.

steps.instruction: Try a steady shape with your arms stretched sideways.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep both feet comfortably grounded; do not time the hold.

steps.instruction: Keep your feet still and try a different arm position.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite a comfortable change, then ask how it feels compared with the first.

steps.instruction: Adjust your arms to make your shape feel steadier.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child decide; neither shape needs to be judged best.

8-10.ending: Relax the shape and describe one adjustment you noticed.

11-12.challenge: Design and adjust a controlled transition between two grounded shapes.

steps.instruction: Choose two comfortable shapes with both feet on the ground.
steps.parent_prompt: Help check space for both shapes and let the child choose arm positions.

steps.instruction: Move slowly between your shapes while keeping your feet grounded.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child pause between shapes; there is no speed or holding target.

steps.instruction: Change one part to make the transition feel steadier.
steps.parent_prompt: Ask whether a smaller arm movement or a pause helps, then try the change.

11-12.ending: Return to rest and name the change that helped you.

simplify: Keep the arms close and use a smaller comfortable range of movement.
extend: Give each existing shape an imaginary name and repeat the same transition.

constraints: Keep both feet on the ground; do not add raised surfaces or one-leg challenges.
Do not add closed eyes, spinning, jumping, pushing or timed holding targets.
Stop or change any movement that feels uncomfortable or unsteady.
Story wording must retain the grounded positions and controlled transitions.

activities.title: Choose Your Route
activities.summary: Plan a short route inside a checked area and guide a partner along it.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks a small, level, clear area with space for a few slow forward steps.
The entire route stays visible and away from traffic, obstacles and moving equipment.
setup: Agree a nearby starting position and a nearby finishing position.
Choose turns only where there is clear space; no signs, lines or markers are required.
Walk together, pause before changing direction and stop whenever wanted.

5-7.challenge: Choose a nearby destination and walk there with an adult.

steps.instruction: Point to a nearby clear spot for us to visit.
steps.parent_prompt: The adult confirms it is inside the checked area.

steps.instruction: Walk beside me to our chosen spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Take a few slow forward steps and stop together.

steps.instruction: Point to our starting spot and walk back with me.
steps.parent_prompt: Turn while stopped, then walk forward rather than backwards.

5-7.ending: Stop together at the starting position and finish.

8-10.challenge: Plan a short route with one stopping point.

steps.instruction: Choose one clear stopping point before our finish.
steps.parent_prompt: Check that both short sections stay inside the agreed area.

steps.instruction: Guide us to the stop and then the finish.
steps.parent_prompt: Pause together before any direction change.

steps.instruction: Choose a different stop and compare the two routes.
steps.parent_prompt: Confirm the new point with the adult before walking.

8-10.ending: Return together to the start and name one route difference.

11-12.challenge: Explain and improve a route for a partner to follow.

steps.instruction: Plan a short route with two clear stopping points.
steps.parent_prompt: Confirm all points and turns within the checked area.

steps.instruction: Give one direction at a time while we walk together.
steps.parent_prompt: Wait at each stopping point before the next instruction.

steps.instruction: Reword one direction to make the route clearer.
steps.parent_prompt: Try that short section together without increasing speed or distance.

11-12.ending: Walk back together and explain which direction became clearer.

simplify: Use one nearby destination with no intermediate stop.
extend: Swap who plans the route within the same checked area.

constraints: Keep the child in the adult's sight and allow pausing or stopping at any time.
Remain together and use slow forward walking; turn only after stopping.
Do not add obstacles, road crossings, hidden destinations or a race.
Future story wording must preserve the tasks, requirements and constraints.

activities.title: Colour Hunt
activities.summary: Look for visible colours together and take turns choosing what to notice.

participation.adult_role: Help choose visible colours and accompany the child within the agreed area.

requirements: An adult checks a permitted observation area away from traffic and active sport.
Colours can be observed without touching objects or entering planting beds.
setup: Agree on a small area where the adult and child will stay together.
Look around together and choose a colour that is actually visible.
Explain that pointing or describing is enough; nothing needs to be collected.
Either person can pause or stop, and an unavailable colour can be changed.

5-7.challenge: Notice one visible colour and take a turn choosing another.

steps.instruction: Point to something with our chosen colour.
steps.parent_prompt: Choose a visible colour together and offer help locating it.

steps.instruction: Point to a different colour you can see.
steps.parent_prompt: Look from the same place or walk together within the agreed area.

steps.instruction: Choose a colour for me to find.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child point out their choice if naming colours is difficult.

5-7.ending: Point to one favourite colour together, then finish the search.

8-10.challenge: Compare two visible colours and use a clue to guide a partner.

steps.instruction: Find two things with colours you can compare.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay together and use visible objects without handling them.

steps.instruction: Describe one colour difference between your two choices.
steps.parent_prompt: Accept the child's description; there is no correct shade to identify.

steps.instruction: Give me a colour clue for one thing you found.
steps.parent_prompt: Take a turn guessing from the checked area; let the child point if needed.

8-10.ending: Reveal the object from the clue and finish the search together.

11-12.challenge: Create a colour comparison rule and adjust it to what is visible.

steps.instruction: Choose a rule for comparing colours you can see.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer examples such as similar shades or a strong contrast; use the child's own descriptions.

steps.instruction: Find two visible examples and explain how they fit your rule.
steps.parent_prompt: Remain together; if examples are unavailable, invite a change to the rule.

steps.instruction: Teach me your rule and help me find another example.
steps.parent_prompt: Ask for a clue and search within the same area, adapting the rule if needed.

11-12.ending: Name one observation the rule helped you make, then finish.

simplify: Point together instead of naming or comparing colours.
Use a visible shape instead of colour if that is easier to distinguish.
extend: Swap who chooses the visible colour or comparison rule for another round.
Describe each observation as an imaginary clue without collecting anything.

constraints: Stay together within the checked area; a clue must never require searching beyond it.
Observe without picking, collecting, tasting or touching unknown objects.
Do not approach animals or strangers to inspect their colours.
Do not assume any particular plant, landmark or colour will be present.
Keep the observation tasks and ending when adding story wording.

activities.title: Follow the Leader
activities.summary: Take turns inventing and copying a short pattern of movements together.

participation.adult_role: Demonstrate, copy the child and help keep movements controlled.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area with room to move without contact.
The area is outside traffic, wheeled routes and play equipment landing areas.
setup: Stand facing each other with enough space to stretch arms without touching.
Agree to use gentle movements such as marching, arm circles or side steps.
Explain that either person can pause, change a movement or stop.

5-7.challenge: Copy one movement at a time and take a turn leading.

steps.instruction: Copy my slow marching steps.
steps.parent_prompt: March gently on the spot; let the child watch before joining.

steps.instruction: Copy my small arm circles.
steps.parent_prompt: Stop marching first, then demonstrate a comfortable arm circle.

steps.instruction: Choose a gentle movement for me to copy.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer the two demonstrated movements if the child wants help choosing.

5-7.ending: Choose one favourite movement and do it together, then stop.

8-10.challenge: Remember a two-movement pattern and notice a change in its order.

steps.instruction: Copy four marching steps, then two small arm circles.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate the whole pattern slowly, then repeat it together.

steps.instruction: Put the arm circles first and try the pattern again.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child organise the two movements; offer a demonstration if wanted.

steps.instruction: Choose two gentle movements and teach me your pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Follow the child's pattern without scoring memory or counting errors.

8-10.ending: Perform the child's two-movement pattern together once, then stop.

11-12.challenge: Design, teach and adapt a three-movement pattern for a partner.

steps.instruction: Choose three gentle movements and arrange them into a pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree which movements fit the space; let the child decide their order.

steps.instruction: Teach me your pattern one movement at a time.
steps.parent_prompt: Copy each movement, then ask the child to lead the combined pattern.

steps.instruction: Change one part so the pattern is easier to copy.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite a change to order, repetition or movement size, then try it together.

11-12.ending: Perform the adapted pattern together once and name the change, then stop.

simplify: Use one comfortable movement at a time and copy it together.
Use small arm movements while staying in place if preferred.
extend: Swap leaders for another round using movements already agreed with the adult.
Give the same movements an imaginary character without adding new actions.

constraints: Keep movements gentle, within the checked area and in the adult's sight.
Do not add climbing, backward travel, chasing, contact or speed competitions.
Do not require equipment, landmarks or surfaces absent from the requirements.
Keep the listed tasks and each age variant's ending when adding story wording.

activities.title: Imaginary Delivery
activities.summary: Pretend to carry a make-believe parcel and decide how to deliver it together.

participation.adult_role: Join the pretend delivery and agree any movements within the checked space.

requirements: An adult checks a small, clear, level area with room for a few forward steps together.
The delivery begins and ends within that area, away from traffic and active play.
setup: Agree on a nearby imaginary delivery spot inside the checked area.
Explain that there is no real parcel to find, pick up or carry.
Use comfortable arm movements and slow forward steps; staying in place is also allowed.
Either person can change the pretend idea, pause or stop.

5-7.challenge: Imagine one parcel and act out delivering it with an adult.

steps.instruction: Pretend you have a soft, light parcel in your hands.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a simple imaginary parcel such as a cushion; nothing is actually held.

steps.instruction: Carry your pretend parcel beside me with slow steps.
steps.parent_prompt: Walk together towards the agreed spot, or mime the delivery in place.

steps.instruction: Show me how you give me the pretend parcel.
steps.parent_prompt: Mime receiving it without requiring touching or carrying any real object.

5-7.ending: Set the imaginary parcel down in the story and relax your arms.

8-10.challenge: Choose an imaginary parcel's shape and adapt how you carry it.

steps.instruction: Choose whether your pretend parcel is wide or narrow.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the imagined parcel light and use only comfortable arm positions.

steps.instruction: Show how you carry that shape to our delivery spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Move together slowly within the checked area or mime the steps in place.

steps.instruction: Pretend its shape changes and adjust your delivery movements.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay at the delivery spot and use smaller arm movements if needed.

8-10.ending: Hand over the pretend parcel and describe how its shape changed your actions.

11-12.challenge: Plan a pretend delivery and adapt it when the imaginary parcel changes.

steps.instruction: Invent a light parcel and explain your delivery plan.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree the nearby destination first; the plan uses the same checked space.

steps.instruction: Act out carrying your parcel towards our agreed delivery spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Walk beside the child with slow forward steps, or perform the delivery in place.

steps.instruction: Imagine its shape changes and decide how to adjust your plan.
steps.parent_prompt: Pause the walking and let the child adapt the arm movements without expanding the area.

steps.instruction: Show your adjusted delivery and explain what you changed.
steps.parent_prompt: Play the receiver and let the child finish using the agreed movements.

11-12.ending: Complete the handover in the story, then return your arms to rest.

simplify: Mime the whole delivery in place with small arm movements.
Let the adult suggest the parcel while the child chooses how to carry it.
extend: Swap sender and receiver roles using the same area and movement limits.

constraints: All parcels are imaginary; do not collect, lift or deliver real objects.
Remain together within the checked area; do not approach strangers as recipients.
Do not add obstacles, roads, water, climbing, running or jumping to the story.
Keep the parcel light in the story and every movement comfortable.
Future story wording must retain the same delivery area and permitted actions.

activities.title: Invisible Orchestra
activities.summary: Invent silent instruments and coordinate gentle playing movements as a pair.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks enough clear space for comfortable hand and arm movements.
setup: Choose imaginary instruments; no real instrument or loud sound is required.
Agree a visible start signal and a rest signal.
Keep movements small, stay in place and stop whenever wanted.

5-7.challenge: Mime one imaginary instrument and pause with a partner.

steps.instruction: Show me how you play an imaginary drum.
steps.parent_prompt: Use small gentle movements in the air without hitting anything.

steps.instruction: Play our silent instruments together.
steps.parent_prompt: Follow the child's comfortable pace; no loud sound is needed.

steps.instruction: Let your instrument rest when I show our signal.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate a gradual comfortable pause.

5-7.ending: Give the rest signal and relax your hands.

8-10.challenge: Give two imaginary instruments distinct movement patterns.

steps.instruction: Choose two silent instruments with different playing movements.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the movements comfortable and within each person's space.

steps.instruction: Alternate between our two instrument movements.
steps.parent_prompt: Use agreed signals so nobody needs to guess which comes next.

steps.instruction: Choose an order for us to play the movements together.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the sequence short and allow a pause between changes.

8-10.ending: Finish the short sequence and let both instruments rest.

11-12.challenge: Arrange and revise a short imaginary performance.

steps.instruction: Assign each of us a silent instrument and a movement pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Make both parts possible with small on-the-spot actions.

steps.instruction: Guide the order of our parts using agreed signals.
steps.parent_prompt: Use a slow pace and a clear rest signal.

steps.instruction: Change one part so our performance is easier to coordinate.
steps.parent_prompt: Try the revised order without scoring rhythm or precision.

11-12.ending: Use the rest signal to end the performance.

simplify: Use one instrument movement and let the adult lead the signals.
extend: Swap the conductor role while keeping the same instruments and signals.

constraints: Keep the child in the adult's sight and allow pausing or stopping at any time.
Do not hit objects, other people or the body to make sounds.
No real instruments, loud calls or vigorous swinging movements are required.
Future story wording must preserve the tasks, requirements and constraints.

activities.title: Listen and Point
activities.summary: Notice sounds from a checked position and describe where they seem to come from.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks a permitted observation area away from traffic and active play.
The activity can use quiet sounds made by the adult if surroundings are quiet.
setup: Stay together with eyes open and listen without leaving the checked area.
Point only from the current position; do not follow a sound to its source.
If listening is uncomfortable, describe visible movement instead or stop.

5-7.challenge: Notice one quiet sound and point towards its apparent direction.

steps.instruction: Listen with me for one quiet sound.
steps.parent_prompt: If needed, make a gentle finger tap where the child can see you.

steps.instruction: Point to where you think the sound comes from.
steps.parent_prompt: Accept the child's guess without checking by approaching anything.

steps.instruction: Choose a sound for us to notice together.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer another quiet tap if no environmental sound is available.

5-7.ending: Name or describe the chosen sound and finish listening.

8-10.challenge: Compare two sounds while remaining in the checked area.

steps.instruction: Notice two sounds or listen to two taps I make.
steps.parent_prompt: Use quiet adult-made sounds if the setting offers none.

steps.instruction: Describe one difference between the two sounds.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite descriptions such as longer or shorter without requiring exact identification.

steps.instruction: Give me a clue about which sound you chose.
steps.parent_prompt: Guess together from the same position.

8-10.ending: Reveal the chosen sound and finish.

11-12.challenge: Create a simple description of the sounds around a checked position.

steps.instruction: Choose how to describe two sounds you notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer apparent direction or length; no sound source needs to be verified.

steps.instruction: Use gestures to show where the sounds seem to come from.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay in place with eyes open and do not follow the sounds.

steps.instruction: Ask how I heard the sounds and compare our descriptions.
steps.parent_prompt: Different impressions are acceptable; use adult-made sounds if needed.

11-12.ending: Choose one shared observation and finish listening.

simplify: Use one quiet visible tap made by the adult.
extend: Repeat from the same position and notice whether the sounds have changed.

constraints: Keep the child in the adult's sight and allow pausing or stopping at any time.
Do not close eyes, follow sounds, approach animals or approach strangers.
Avoid loud sounds and stop if listening is uncomfortable.
Future story wording must preserve the tasks, requirements and constraints.

activities.title: Notice the Change
activities.summary: Take turns changing a small part of a pose and noticing what is different.

participation.adult_role: Show small pose changes, keep the child in sight and offer clues when wanted.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area where the pair can stand without contact.
Both people can observe each other without blocking routes or active play.
setup: Face each other with enough room for small arm movements.
Agree to stay in place and change only comfortable hand or arm positions.
When a change is hidden, the child looks to one side with eyes open and stays still.
Either person can request a clue, pass a turn or finish the activity.

5-7.challenge: Notice one visible change and then choose a change yourself.

steps.instruction: Watch my hands and point to what changes.
steps.parent_prompt: Slowly change one hand from open to closed while the child watches.

steps.instruction: Tell me or show me which hand changed.
steps.parent_prompt: Show the original and new positions again if the child wants help.

steps.instruction: Change one hand position for me to notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Describe what you see; the child does not need to copy your example.

5-7.ending: Reveal the last change and return both hands to rest.

8-10.challenge: Remember a pose and identify one change after looking away.

steps.instruction: Look at my arm positions, then look to one side.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay nearby with the child in sight; change one small arm position.

steps.instruction: Look back and describe the change you notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a clue or show both poses again; guessing is optional.

steps.instruction: Choose one pose change for me to spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Look at the child's feet while they change one arm, keeping them in sight.

8-10.ending: Explain the final change to each other and return to rest.

11-12.challenge: Compare two pose changes and choose a useful clue for an observer.

steps.instruction: Study my hand and arm positions, then look to one side.
steps.parent_prompt: Make two small comfortable changes while keeping the child in sight.

steps.instruction: Look back and explain the two differences you notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a comparison with the original pose; there is no score for recall.

steps.instruction: Choose a pose change and a clue to help me notice it.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the child in sight while looking at their feet, then look up and use the clue.

11-12.ending: Reveal the change and explain how the clue helped, then relax.

simplify: Make one slow change while the observer watches the whole time.
Point or demonstrate instead of describing the change in words.
extend: Swap who invents the change and who gives a clue for another round.

constraints: Stay in place with eyes open; do not add hiding, blindfolds or searching elsewhere.
The adult must keep the child in sight throughout each turn.
Change only comfortable hand or arm positions; do not require contact or props.
Story wording must preserve the observation and comparison tasks.

activities.title: Opposite Actions
activities.summary: Use agreed pairs of gentle actions to respond with the opposite movement.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks clear space for small arm movements while both feet stay grounded.
setup: Agree a simple pair such as arms apart and arms close.
Demonstrate both actions before trying the opposite rule.
Allow a demonstration, a pause or a skipped turn whenever wanted.

5-7.challenge: Respond with the other action from one familiar pair.

steps.instruction: Show arms apart, then bring them close.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate within a comfortable range with both feet grounded.

steps.instruction: When my arms open, bring yours close.
steps.parent_prompt: Show the expected response slowly; this is not a speed test.

steps.instruction: Choose one arm position for me to answer.
steps.parent_prompt: Respond with the other agreed position.

5-7.ending: Show both agreed positions together and finish.

8-10.challenge: Apply the opposite rule while taking turns choosing actions.

steps.instruction: Choose two different gentle arm positions for our pair.
steps.parent_prompt: Use positions that fit the space and feel comfortable.

steps.instruction: Show the other position when I show one.
steps.parent_prompt: Pause to think or ask for the pair to be demonstrated again.

steps.instruction: Lead three turns using either position from our pair.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep each turn separate with time for the partner to respond.

8-10.ending: Relax your arms and explain the pair you used.

11-12.challenge: Explain and adapt an opposite-action rule for a partner.

steps.instruction: Choose two pairs of comfortable hand or arm positions.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate the pairs with the adult before adding a rule.

steps.instruction: Name a pair, show one position and ask for its opposite.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the pair named aloud so the partner need not guess which rule applies.

steps.instruction: Change the rule if it is difficult to follow.
steps.parent_prompt: Use one pair or a demonstration rather than adding speed.

11-12.ending: Try the agreed simpler rule once, then finish.

simplify: Use one pair and demonstrate the response on every turn.
extend: Swap who chooses the agreed pair for another round.

constraints: Keep the child in the adult's sight and allow pausing or stopping at any time.
Keep both feet on the ground and use comfortable arm or hand positions.
Do not introduce punishment, elimination or timed responses.
Future story wording must preserve the tasks, requirements and constraints.

activities.title: Partner Ball Carry
activities.summary: Support a soft ball together and coordinate a few slow steps as a pair.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

required: A soft ball large enough for the child and adult to support together.

requirements: An adult checks a small, clear, level area for a few slow forward steps together.
Both participants can support the ball comfortably without gripping each other.
setup: Agree a comfortable position beside each other and try supporting the ball while still.
The adult supports most of the weight and can catch or lower the ball.
If the ball drops, stop and wait; either person can pause or finish.

5-7.challenge: Support the ball together and coordinate one gentle step.

steps.instruction: Help me support our soft ball.
steps.parent_prompt: Use comfortable hand positions and avoid touching or gripping the child.

steps.instruction: Take one slow step forward beside me.
steps.parent_prompt: The adult guides the pace within the checked space.

steps.instruction: Stop with me and hold the ball still.
steps.parent_prompt: Allow the child to release their hands whenever wanted.

5-7.ending: Let the adult take the ball and return to rest.

8-10.challenge: Agree and use a shared signal for moving and pausing.

steps.instruction: Choose a word that tells us to take a step.
steps.parent_prompt: Practise while the adult securely supports the ball.

steps.instruction: Use our signal for a few slow steps together.
steps.parent_prompt: Walk forwards beside each other and stop between signals.

steps.instruction: Choose how to make our next shared step easier.
steps.parent_prompt: Try a smaller step or a longer pause, not a greater distance.

8-10.ending: Pause together and let the adult take the ball.

11-12.challenge: Plan and adapt a short cooperative carry.

steps.instruction: Agree nearby start and finish positions and a shared pace.
steps.parent_prompt: The adult checks the short route and comfortable shared support.

steps.instruction: Guide us through a few slow steps with the ball.
steps.parent_prompt: Use agreed signals and remain beside each other.

steps.instruction: Change the signals or step size to improve coordination.
steps.parent_prompt: Try the adjustment within the same checked area; success is not scored.

11-12.ending: Let the adult take the ball and describe one helpful adjustment.

simplify: Support the ball together while staying still.
extend: Swap who gives the stepping signals for another short carry.

constraints: Keep the child in the adult's sight and allow pausing or stopping at any time.
Do not lift the ball overhead or add racing, balancing tricks or body contact.
If the ball drops, stop rather than chasing; the adult retrieves it when appropriate.
Future story wording must preserve the tasks, requirements and constraints.

activities.title: Pass and Move
activities.summary: Roll a soft ball to a partner, then change position together for the next pass.

participation.adult_role: Roll the ball gently, agree each position and retrieve loose balls only when appropriate.

required: A soft ball suitable for rolling between the child and adult.

requirements: An adult checks a level, clear area where a ball can roll without entering traffic or active play.
There is room for the pair to change position without contacting other people.
The family brings the ball; the location dataset does not establish equipment availability.
setup: Face each other a short, comfortable rolling distance apart.
Agree to roll along the ground and stop the ball before changing position.
Agree that the child will wait if the ball leaves the checked area.
Either person can pause, move closer or end the game at any point.

5-7.challenge: Stop and return a gentle roll, then move to an agreed position.

steps.instruction: Stop the ball I roll towards you.
steps.parent_prompt: Roll gently from nearby and let the child choose a comfortable way to stop it.

steps.instruction: Roll the ball back towards me.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay close and make the receiving position easy to see.

steps.instruction: Hold the ball while we each take one sideways step.
steps.parent_prompt: Check room first, move together, then stop and exchange another gentle roll.

5-7.ending: Stop the ball after one final exchange and finish together.

8-10.challenge: Compare two rolling distances and choose one that helps the pair cooperate.

steps.instruction: Exchange two gentle rolls from our starting positions.
steps.parent_prompt: Stop the ball between turns and count exchanges together without scoring.

steps.instruction: Hold the ball while we choose a second rolling distance.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree a small change within the checked area, stop moving, then exchange two rolls.

steps.instruction: Choose which distance made the ball easier to control.
steps.parent_prompt: Move to the chosen positions while holding the ball, then try another exchange.

8-10.ending: Stop the ball and describe which distance worked for you both.

11-12.challenge: Plan and improve a short pattern of positions for cooperative rolling.

steps.instruction: Choose two nearby positions for our rolling pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree positions within the checked area; no markers or field lines are needed.

steps.instruction: Guide us through one exchange at each position.
steps.parent_prompt: Hold the ball during every position change and roll only when both people are still.

steps.instruction: Change one position to make the next exchange easier to control.
steps.parent_prompt: Discuss the change, move while holding the ball and repeat the adjusted pattern.

11-12.ending: Stop the ball after the adjusted pattern and name the change together.

simplify: Stay in one position and shorten the distance between partners.
Stop each roll with help from the adult before taking another turn.
extend: Swap who chooses the positions while keeping the same checked area and rolling rules.
Treat the same gentle rolls as delivering an imaginary parcel.

constraints: Roll on the ground; do not add throwing, kicking, striking or speed targets.
Stop and hold the ball before changing position; do not chase a moving ball.
If the ball leaves the checked area, the child waits with the activity paused.
Do not assume nets, hoops, painted lines, markers or supplied equipment.
Keep the rolling and position-change rules when adding story wording.

activities.title: Rhythm Steps
activities.summary: Match comfortable stepping to a short rhythm and build a pattern together.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area with room to step on the spot.
setup: Agree to use gentle marching or side steps within the checked area.
Use a quiet spoken rhythm; no music device is needed.
Either person can pause, simplify the pattern or stop.

5-7.challenge: Match one gentle step to each spoken beat.

steps.instruction: Take one gentle marching step for each beat I say.
steps.parent_prompt: Say a slow, even beat and demonstrate on the spot.

steps.instruction: Stand still when we leave a quiet gap.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the pause predictable and let the child watch your demonstration.

steps.instruction: Choose a short rhythm for our steps.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer two gentle beats and a pause if the child wants an idea.

5-7.ending: Finish your short rhythm together and return to rest.

activities.title: Robot Instructions
activities.summary: Give a pretend robot a short sequence of gentle movements and improve the instructions.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks clear, level space for small movements on the spot.
setup: Agree that the adult or child can play a pretend robot.
Choose permitted actions such as an arm movement, marching in place or resting.

5-7.challenge: Give a pretend robot one clear movement instruction.

steps.instruction: Tell my robot arms to open or close.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate a comfortable range with both feet grounded.

steps.instruction: Watch me try your instruction.
steps.parent_prompt: Respond slowly and ask for a demonstration if the instruction is unclear.

steps.instruction: Try being the robot while I give one instruction.
steps.parent_prompt: Use only the already agreed gentle actions.

8-10.challenge: Plan and test a two-instruction sequence for a robot.

steps.instruction: Choose two gentle robot actions in an order.
steps.parent_prompt: Confirm that both actions fit the space.

steps.instruction: Give one command at a time while I act it out.
steps.parent_prompt: Pause between commands so both people can check the sequence.

steps.instruction: Change one instruction that was hard to understand.
steps.parent_prompt: Replay the two actions slowly using the clearer wording.

8-10.ending: Tell the robot to rest and describe the clearer command.

11-12.challenge: Design and revise a short instruction sequence.

steps.instruction: Plan three agreed robot actions and explain their order.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep every action on the spot with controlled movements.

steps.instruction: Guide the robot through your commands one at a time.
steps.parent_prompt: Follow the instructions as understood; clarify without inventing risky actions.

steps.instruction: Change the order or wording to improve the sequence.
steps.parent_prompt: Try the revised plan with no speed or performance score.

extend: Swap robot and guide for another short sequence of agreed actions.

activities.title: Roll to Target
activities.summary: Roll a soft ball towards a family-supplied target and adjust direction or distance.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

required: A soft ball suitable for rolling.
A large cloth target placed flat by the adult, outside walking routes.

requirements: An adult checks a level rolling area where a ball cannot enter traffic or active play.
The cloth can lie flat and all walking remains clear of it.
setup: Place the cloth at a short comfortable rolling distance.
Agree to roll along the ground and wait for the ball to stop.
The child waits if the ball leaves the checked area; the game can pause or stop.

5-7.challenge: Roll towards a clear nearby target and try again from the same place.

steps.instruction: Point to our cloth target.
steps.parent_prompt: Confirm that the target is family-supplied and lies away from feet.

steps.instruction: Roll the ball gently towards the cloth.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate from nearby without requiring the ball to hit the target.

steps.instruction: Choose whether to try again or move closer with me.
steps.parent_prompt: Hold the stopped ball before repositioning.

5-7.ending: Stop the ball and collect the supplied equipment with the adult.

8-10.challenge: Compare two rolling directions and choose an adjustment.

steps.instruction: Try one gentle roll towards the cloth.
steps.parent_prompt: Wait for the ball to stop; do not chase it.

steps.instruction: Choose how to change your next rolling direction.
steps.parent_prompt: Discuss the result without counting hits or misses.

steps.instruction: Try your adjustment from the same position.
steps.parent_prompt: Use the same gentle force and a short comfortable distance.

8-10.ending: Stop the ball and explain what you adjusted.

11-12.challenge: Plan and compare a direction or distance adjustment.

steps.instruction: Choose a nearby rolling position and explain your aim.
steps.parent_prompt: The adult checks that the entire roll remains in the agreed area.

steps.instruction: Try a gentle roll and describe where it stopped.
steps.parent_prompt: Retrieve only after the ball stops and remain clear of the cloth.

steps.instruction: Change direction or distance and compare your next roll.
steps.parent_prompt: Hold the ball while repositioning and avoid speed or accuracy scoring.

11-12.ending: Stop the ball, name one observation and collect the equipment.

simplify: Move closer to the cloth with the stopped ball held.
extend: Take another planning turn with the same target inside the checked area.

activities.title: Silent Scene
activities.summary: Mime a familiar everyday action and help a partner understand the scene.

requirements: An adult checks clear, level space for small on-the-spot actions.
setup: Agree familiar pretend actions that need no props, such as opening a book.

steps.instruction: Show me how you open an imaginary book.
steps.parent_prompt: Mime the action gently; no real object is held.

steps.parent_prompt: Choose another agreed familiar action and accept different interpretations.

steps.instruction: Choose a pretend action for me to recognise.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer two familiar choices if the child wants help.

8-10.challenge: Combine two familiar actions into a short scene.

steps.instruction: Choose two everyday actions that belong in one scene.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree small on-the-spot movements without props.

steps.instruction: Show the actions in order while I watch.
steps.parent_prompt: Give the child time; recognising the scene is not scored.

steps.instruction: Change one gesture to help explain your scene.
steps.parent_prompt: The child can also describe the idea aloud if preferred.

11-12.challenge: Design a scene and revise its gestures after a partner's interpretation.

steps.parent_prompt: Confirm that the scene needs no real objects, travel or contact.

steps.instruction: Act out your scene and ask what I understood.

steps.parent_prompt: Repeat just the adjusted part and compare interpretations.

activities.title: Sort and Step
activities.summary: Sort familiar picture cards by a chosen rule and move between nearby groups.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

required: At least four large familiar picture cards brought by the family.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area for two nearby card groups and forward steps.

setup: Choose a few family-supplied cards with pictures the child recognises.
Place groups beside the walking space, not under anyone's feet.
Pause or stop whenever wanted; the adult handles cards if preferred.

5-7.challenge: Use one simple rule to place familiar pictures into two groups.

steps.instruction: Choose pictures of animals and pictures of other things.
steps.parent_prompt: Use suitable cards brought by the family; demonstrate the two groups.

steps.instruction: Point to the group where this card belongs.
steps.parent_prompt: The adult places the card and walks beside the child to that group.

steps.instruction: Choose another card and show me its group.
steps.parent_prompt: Use a few slow forward steps between the checked positions.

5-7.ending: Look at the two groups together, then collect the supplied cards.

8-10.challenge: Explain a sorting rule and apply it to unfamiliar choices.

steps.instruction: Choose a rule for making two groups from our cards.
steps.parent_prompt: Help choose a rule that fits the actual supplied pictures.

steps.instruction: Decide where each card goes and walk with me to its group.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep cards beside the walking space and turn only while stopped.

steps.instruction: Explain a card that could fit more than one group.
steps.parent_prompt: Allow either choice when the child explains their reasoning.

activities.title: Step and Pause

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks level space for comfortable marching on the spot.
setup: Agree that 'move' means gentle marching and 'pause' means a comfortable stop.

activities.title: Viewpoint Switch
activities.summary: Compare how a visible feature looks from two nearby checked positions.

participation.adult_role: Explain the game, participate and keep the child within the checked area.

requirements: An adult checks two nearby, clear, level observation positions.
A visible feature can be observed from both positions without touching or approaching hazards.
setup: Choose a feature actually visible from the checked area.
Agree the short forward-walking route between the two positions.
If there is no suitable second position, compare from one position or stop.

5-7.challenge: Look at one visible feature from two positions beside an adult.

steps.instruction: Point to something we can see from here.
steps.parent_prompt: Help choose a feature that does not require approaching animals or people.

steps.instruction: Walk beside me to our other checked spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Use a few slow steps with the adult.

steps.instruction: Point to the same thing from this spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Ask what the child notices without requiring a technical explanation.

5-7.ending: Choose a favourite view and finish the observation.

8-10.challenge: Compare one visible feature from two nearby positions.

steps.instruction: Describe one detail you can see from here.
steps.parent_prompt: Use an existing feature without handling anything.

steps.parent_prompt: Stay on the agreed clear route.

steps.instruction: Explain what looks different or stays the same.
steps.parent_prompt: Accept that nothing may change noticeably; either result is useful.
